title_en: Who did it? Nobody says: the passive
q_en: The door was opened. By whom? The sentence does not say. How does Arabic say it?
q_ar: فُتِحَ الْبَابُ. مَنْ فَتَحَهُ؟ لَا تَقُولُ الْجُمْلَةُ. كَيْفَ تَقُولُ الْعَرَبِيَّةُ ذَلِكَ؟
not_yet: Passives of the other verb shapes (Forms II–X): later, one at a time.
Passives of weak verbs (قَالَ, وَلَدَ): only the whole words قِيلَ, وُلِدَ, يُقَالُ.
Passive with a doer shown (by whom): we only say the doer is hidden.
not_yet_ar: الْمَجْهُولُ مِنْ بَقِيَّةِ الْأَوْزَانِ (الثَّانِي إِلَى الْعَاشِرِ): فِي دُرُوسٍ قَادِمَةٍ، وَاحِدًا وَاحِدًا.
الْمَجْهُولُ مِنَ الْأَفْعَالِ الْمُعْتَلَّةِ (قَالَ، وَلَدَ): نَتَعَلَّمُ فَقَطْ قِيلَ وَوُلِدَ وَيُقَالُ كَامِلَةً.
ذِكْرُ الْفَاعِلِ مَعَ الْمَجْهُولِ: نَقُولُ هُنَا إِنَّ الْفَاعِلَ مَحْذُوفٌ فَقَطْ.

slides.head_en: Look: one event, told two ways

lines: In the second sentence, who opened the door? Does the sentence say?

Look at the verb. What happened to its first letter, and to the vowel before its last letter?
اُنْظُرْ إِلَى الْفِعْلِ: مَاذَا حَدَثَ لِحَرْفِهِ الْأَوَّلِ وَلِلْحَرَكَةِ قَبْلَ حَرْفِهِ الْأَخِيرِ؟
Look at الْبَابَ and الْبَابُ. What happened to the ending, and why?
اُنْظُرْ إِلَى «الْبَابَ» وَ«الْبَابُ»: مَاذَا حَدَثَ لِلنِّهَايَةِ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟

cards.def_en: We do not say who did it.
Past: ḍamma, then kasra. Present: يُـ, then fatḥa.
What it happened to takes the doer’s place: ḍamma.
he was born · it is said · it was said

slides.head_en: The system: active and passive, past and present
slides.note: Same root, same letters: only the vowels change.
slides.note_ar: الْجَذْرُ هُوَ هُوَ وَالْحُرُوفُ هِيَ هِيَ: تَتَغَيَّرُ الْحَرَكَاتُ فَقَطْ.

slides.head_en: When do we use the passive?
slides.big_en: When the doer is unknown, obvious, or not important.
slides.big_ar: فُتِحَ الْبَابُ  ·  كُتِبَ الدَّرْسُ  ·  وُلِدَ أَحْمَدُ
slides.small: The sentence keeps what happened and drops who did it. The one it happened to now leads the sentence.
slides.small_ar: تَحْفَظُ الْجُمْلَةُ مَا حَدَثَ وَتَتْرُكُ مَنْ فَعَلَ. وَيَتَقَدَّمُ مَنْ وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ الْفِعْلُ.

slides.why: A student writes فُتِحَ الْبَابَ for “the door was opened”. Wrong! With a passive verb the door is no longer the object: it is now what the sentence is about, so it takes ḍamma: فُتِحَ الْبَابُ.
slides.why_ar: كَتَبَ طَالِبٌ «فُتِحَ الْبَابَ». هَذَا خَطَأٌ! الْبَابُ هُوَ الَّذِي تَتَحَدَّثُ عَنْهُ الْجُمْلَةُ الْآنَ، فَيَكُونُ بِالضَّمَّةِ: فُتِحَ الْبَابُ.

sections.name: A
sections.en: Read the story, then answer.
lines: سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ عُمَرَ: أَيْنَ وُلِدَ إِمَامُ الْمَسْجِدِ؟
Ahmad asked ʿUmar: Where was the imam of the mosque born?
قَالَ عُمَرُ: يُقَالُ إِنَّهُ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ، وَطَلَبَ الْعِلْمَ هُنَاكَ.
ʿUmar said: It is said that he was born in Tarim, and that he sought knowledge there.
قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: وَأَيْنَ يُطْلَبُ الْعِلْمُ الْيَوْمَ؟
Ahmad said: And where is knowledge sought today?
قَالَ عُمَرُ: يُطْلَبُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ وَفِي الْمَسْجِدِ، وَتُفْتَحُ أَبْوَابُ الْمَسْجِدِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
ʿUmar said: It is sought in the ribāṭ and in the mosque, and the doors of the mosque are opened in the morning.
ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدَانِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ، وَسُمِعَ الذِّكْرُ مِنْ بَعِيدٍ.
Then the two boys went to the mosque, and the dhikr was heard from far away.
قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: كُتِبَ هَذَا الدَّرْسُ فِي كِتَابٍ قَدِيمٍ، وَحُفِظَ فِي الْقُلُوبِ.
Ahmad said: This lesson was written in an old book, and it was memorised in the hearts.
قَالَ عُمَرُ: وَقِيلَ لَنَا: اِحْفَظُوا الدَّرْسَ.
ʿUmar said: And it was said to us: Memorise the lesson.

sections.name: Y
sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–72
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
